basis.governing_question: How can Iberia Foods identify savings of 8% of its cost base without cutting service levels?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Diagnose the cost base across twelve workstreams and design the program to identify savings of 8% without cutting service levels.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the savings findings and program design as the final result?

workstreams.name: Procurement
workstreams.answers: What does Iberia Foods spend on bought goods and services, and where could spend fall without lowering service levels?
activities: Analyze spend data by category and supplier
Interview buyers and internal users of purchased items
Size savings options and design how to deliver them

workstreams.name: Manufacturing
workstreams.answers: What does production cost, and where could that cost fall without lowering service levels?
activities: Analyze production cost data by process step
Interview line staff and supervisors on cost drivers
Size savings options and design how to deliver them

workstreams.name: Logistics
workstreams.answers: What do transport and delivery cost, and where could that cost fall without lowering service levels?
activities: Analyze transport cost and delivery performance data
Interview the people who plan and make deliveries
Size savings options and design how to deliver them

workstreams.name: Sales and marketing
workstreams.answers: What do selling and marketing activities cost, and which could cost less without lowering service levels?
activities: Analyze sales and marketing spend against sales results
Interview customers on what selling support they value
Size savings options and design how to deliver them

workstreams.name: Finance
workstreams.answers: What is the verified cost base, including finance's own cost, and what do all sized savings add up to?
activities: Build the cost base from financial records
Interview finance staff on how costs are recorded
Reconcile each stream's sized savings to the cost base

workstreams.name: Customer service
workstreams.answers: What do customer service activities cost, and what service levels must other savings leave intact?
activities: Interview customers on the service levels they rely on
Analyze service performance and customer contact data
Test other streams' savings options against service levels

workstreams.name: Warehousing
workstreams.answers: What do storage and handling cost, and where could that cost fall without lowering service levels?
activities: Analyze storage cost and stock handling data
Interview the people who handle stock and orders
Size savings options and design how to deliver them

workstreams.name: Pricing
workstreams.answers: How do pricing practices relate to the cost of serving customers, and what could change without lowering service levels?
activities: Review pricing documents and sales data by customer
Interview the people who set and apply prices
Size savings options and design how to deliver them

workstreams.name: HR
workstreams.answers: What do HR activities and workforce arrangements cost, and which could change without lowering service levels?
activities: Analyze workforce cost and staffing data by activity
Interview managers and staff on how work is organized
Size savings options and test them against service levels

workstreams.name: IT
workstreams.answers: What do IT services and systems cost, and which could change without lowering service levels?
activities: Analyze IT cost data by service and user group
Interview IT staff and the users of its services
Size savings options and the IT support other streams need

workstreams.name: Legal
workstreams.answers: What do legal services cost, and which contractual commitments constrain savings in other streams?
activities: Review contracts and commitments that limit savings
Analyze legal service cost data by type of matter
Interview contract owners in the other streams

workstreams.name: Real estate
workstreams.answers: What do property and sites cost, and which could change without lowering service levels?
activities: Analyze property cost and space use data
Interview the people who use and manage the sites
Size savings options and test them against service levels

deliverables.name: Spend baseline by category and supplier
Procurement savings options and delivery plan
Production cost savings options and delivery plan
Logistics cost savings options and delivery plan
Sales and marketing savings options and delivery plan
Verified cost base from financial records
Reconciled savings against the cost base
Warehousing savings options and delivery plan
Pricing savings options and delivery plan
HR and workforce savings options and delivery plan
IT savings options and support other streams need
Property and sites savings options and delivery plan

events.label: Kick-off
events.decision: Confirm the scope, team and calendar for the 12-week cost diagnostic?
agenda: Present the diagnostic scope, workstreams and deliverables
Confirm the team and the steering calendar
Align on the 8% savings goal and the service-level condition

events.label: Workshop 1: cost base
events.purpose: Review cost base and service levels
events.decision: Confirm the verified cost base and service levels as the baseline for savings options?
agenda: Present the verified cost base from financial records
Review the service levels customers rely on
Align on how savings options will be tested against service levels

events.label: Workshop 2: spend, limits
events.purpose: Review spend baseline and contract limits
events.decision: Which cost areas should the team detail into savings options and delivery plans?
agenda: Present the spend baseline by category and supplier
Review contractual commitments that limit savings
Discuss emerging savings areas against the 8% target

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Close the diagnostic and approve the result
events.decision: Approve the savings findings and program design as the final result?
agenda: Present savings options and delivery plans by workstream
Review reconciled savings against the cost base and service levels
Decide whether to approve the findings and program design

architect_notes: Twelve workstreams cap the plan at one phase, so the diagnostic and design stages the brief names are planned as one 12-week phase.
The phase is named Diagnostic as the closest fit for a combined diagnostic-and-design stage; no separate Design phase appears.
Performance improvement archetype used; its Implementation phase is dropped because the engagement is an assessment with no implementation support.
No stream owns the cross-stream program design; Finance reconciles savings to the cost base and each stream designs its own part.
